$comment: v0.10-P2-A · Phase A of the DESIGN-SYSTEM-ROADMAP.md uplift.
Single source of truth for every brand / surface / typography
decision made anywhere in PixCull's three rendering targets:
• Web   — results.html + upload.html + admin/*
• iOS   — mobile/PixCullCompanion/Sources/...
• PDF   — cli_audit --executive + executive_pdf.py
Editable by designers via Tokens Studio (a Figma plugin) — the
JSON shape mirrors their schema.  Engineers consume the output
of `python scripts/build_design_tokens.py` which converts this
file into the three platform-specific targets at build time.
DO NOT edit the generated *.css / *.swift files — edits will be
overwritten on the next build.  Edit THIS file.
v3.66 — reconciled with what the product actually ships.
This block used to hold #c4b9a9 / #988b78 / #6a6052 under the
names indigo / violet / pink: a desaturated mid-flight copy of
the warm palette, wearing the names of the purple ramp it had
replaced.  docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md ask 5 framed that as a three-way
choice between this file, results.html and pixcull-brand.json.
It was not a three-way choice.  results.html's own tokens.css
already calls #d5b584 `--accent` and names it champagne gold;
pixcull-brand.json's lighter ramp is keyed wordmarkStart/Mid/End
and is a DIFFERENT ROLE (a wordmark gradient on a dark banner),
not a competing opinion.  Only this file held a value nothing
renders.  So: adopt the shipped ramp, add the wordmark ramp as
the role it is, and nothing a user sees changes.

champagne.description: The accent. Shipped as `--accent` in results.html; oklch(0.790 0.075 78). Every accented control, the keep ring, the focus ring.

champagne-mid.comment: v3.72 — the ramp's middle step. It was always in the product, as a literal in every three-stop brand gradient, and never a token.

champagne-hi.description: Accent, lifted — `--accent-hi`, accent + 0.064 L. Hover and the brighter half of the gradient.

champagne-deep.description: Accent, dropped — the far end of the brand gradient and the colour of an accent border on a light ground.

gradient.description: The signature gradient, exactly as results.html emits it. Avoid using it anywhere except the v0.9-defined signature surfaces (logo, primary CTA, hero numerals, loading bar).

wordmark-start.description: Wordmark ramp stop 1. A separate role from the accent: this ramp is drawn on the dark banner and hero, where the accent ramp would sit too close to the ground. From scripts/brand/pixcull-brand.json, which the brand kit renders.

wordmark-gradient.description: What PixCull's own name is filled with in docs/brand/*.svg.

bg.description: App background — warm espresso ground (v2.3 editorial-warm)

surface-3.description: Inset blocks (e.g. inspector cell, code blocks)

$comment: v3.66 — taken from the shipped page, not re-derived here.
results.html computes these live in OKLCH (accent-hi = accent
+ 0.064 L, soft = 16% alpha, glow = 40%, focus-ring = accent-hi
at 55%) and carries the same values as literals in its
@supports-not fallback. These ARE those literals.

out.description: PixCull-Overshoot — the signature curve. 6% overshoot at y≈1.04, settles at 1.00. Same family as Linear/Stripe/Apple Photos. Used on 200+ transitions; the brand's motion identity.

pixcull-overshoot.description: Canonical name for the signature curve. Use this name in any new CSS over ease.out for clarity.

out-flat.description: PixCull-Overshoot-Flat — use ONLY where overshoot would mislead the user (data-bar widths, progress fills).

in-out.description: Linear-symmetric ease. Modal entrance + exit when both sides need to mirror.

spring.description: Alias of ease.out / pixcull-overshoot — kept for legacy CSS references.

_themes.$comment: v3.73 (Phase A.1) — the light theme, measured. Every value here was read out of a rendered results.html with the theme applied, not derived: the product computes its palette with relative oklch() and arithmetic on the source would have produced numbers that look right and are not what ships. The block above holds the dark theme, which is the default. Regenerate with scripts/measure_theme_tokens.py.
